result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would remove the evolutionary hardwiring that makes humans instinctively fear and distrust the unfamiliar. 

Much of the world’s suffering—war, bigotry, greed, and cruelty—stems from a primitive, tribal urge to protect "us" by destroying or subjugating "them." We are wired for scarcity, zero-sum games, and immediate in-group loyalty in a reality that now demands global cooperation and empathy. 

If that single psychological baseline were rewritten—so that the immediate, visceral reaction to difference was curiosity rather than threat, and empathy was as automatic as self-preservation—humanity would finally be able to build a truly cooperative civilization. We could solve climate change, poverty, and systemic injustice almost overnight, because we would finally see one another as part of the same whole, rather than competitors for a finite existence.
